chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: The blood money (diyah) is inherited by the heirs according to the shares of inheritance, except for the brothers from the mother, for they do not inherit anything from the blood money.
ai.seo_question: Do maternal brothers inherit blood money (diyah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while the general distribution of blood money (diyah) follows the standard Quranic inheritance shares, maternal brothers are uniquely excluded from this compensation. This ruling highlights a distinct jurisprudential nuance in Shia fiqh, distinguishing the rights to financial compensation for homicide from the general rules of inheritance, thereby preventing the dilution of the primary heirs' shares.
